item.title: SCIg for Primary Immunodeficiency: Troubleshooting Swelling, Redness, and Pain at the Infusion Site
item.description: Discover tips for managing swelling, redness, and pain at subcutaneous immunoglobulin (SCIg) infusion sites for primary immunodeficiency therapy. Learn when to seek professional help.

item.title: 7 Tips to Beat Brain Fog
item.description: Brain fog, or limited cognitive function, may be caused by stress, poor sleep, and other factors. Here are some tips to manage mental fatigue.

item.title: 6 Ovarian Cancer Myths to Stop Believing Immediately
item.description: Separate facts and misconceptions about ovarian cancer to help better prevent and manage the disease.

item.title: 5 Flu Shot Myths to Stop Believing Now
item.description: Doctors want you to stop believing flu shot myths and to protect your health. Read on for accurate information on how flu vaccines work.

item.title: Can Creatine Supplements Cause Weight Gain?
item.description: You might notice your weight increase slightly after starting to supplement with creatine, but this initial weight gain doesn’t necessarily translate to an increase in fat mass. Here’s what to know.

item.title: Can You Still Eat Cereal if You Have Type 2 Diabetes?
item.description: Learn more about which types of cereal to pour into your bowl for a healthy breakfast that won’t start your day with higher blood sugar levels.

item.title: Types of Down Syndrome
item.description: Get to know the three types of Down syndrome and how the genetic condition’s characteristics can differ from person to person.

item.description: Dietitians share their top 7 smoothie ingredients for maximum nutrition, from antioxidant-rich dragon fruit to protein-packed cottage cheese.

item.title: What to Know About Catherine O’Hara’s Rare Heart Condition
item.description: The actress was born with her heart on the right side of her chest, not the left. It’s not known if this condition has any link to O’Hara’s death last week.

item.title: Is Salt Good for You?
item.description: Salt, or sodium chloride, is an important source of sodium, an essential nutrient your body needs to function. However, consuming too much salt can have negative effects on your health.
